title: The statutory drug store permit: required to keep a store open, displayed, issued on a 150-day decision and expiring in uneven-numbered years
subtopic: Drug store permit under M.G.L. c. 112, ss. 38 and 39
rule_summary: Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 38 no store, retail food store pharmacy department or retail store pharmacy department shall be kept open for the transaction of the retail drug business, or be advertised or represented as transacting that business by a sign or advertisement containing the words drug store, pharmacy, apothecary, drug, drugs or medicine shop, or any combination of them, or otherwise, unless it is registered with, and a permit for it has been issued by, the Board; with the written permission of the Board those words may be used for an unregistered store if there is no registered store in the town, or voting precinct of the town, where it is located, and town does not include city. The permit shall be displayed in a conspicuous place in the store or department for which it is issued. Under s. 39 the Board may, on application made in the manner and form it determines, register a store or department and issue to the person it deems qualified a permit to keep it open; it may deny registration and refuse the permit if, in its reasonable discretion, the store would be inconsistent with or opposed to the best interests of the public health, welfare or safety; and no registration shall be made or permit issued to a corporation unless the Board is satisfied that management is in the hands of a registered pharmacist. The permit shall expire on December 31 of each uneven numbered year following the date of its issue, with the fee determined annually under M.G.L. c. 7, s. 3B. The Board shall render a final decision denying or allowing registration within 150 days after the filing of an application.
exam_relevance: Tests that the statute, not only the regulation, ties keeping a store open to a Board permit, and fixes the uneven-year expiry, the display duty and the 150-day decision period.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39, first and second paragraphs

numeric_facts.value: December 31 of each uneven numbered year following issue

numeric_facts.fact: Board final decision on an application for registration
numeric_facts.conditions: after the filing of the application

exceptions: With the written permission of the Board the listed words may be used for an unregistered store if no registered store exists in the town, or voting precinct of the town, where it is located; town does not include city.
common_confusions: Section 39 states a 150-day period for the Board's final decision but, unlike s. 39B for a nuclear pharmacy, does not say that a failure to decide is an approval.
A corporation may hold the permit only if management of the store is in the hands of a registered pharmacist.
